claims.text: The starting catalyst is a high-entropy automotive alloy containing nearly equiatomic PGM elements such as Pd, Pt, and Rh together with base metals such as Co and Ni.
The starting catalyst suffers activity loss, thermal-aging degradation, and durability problems under transient, low-temperature gasoline or hybrid exhaust conditions.
The proposed intervention is one cyclic redox pretreatment at approximately 250–350 °C in lean gas containing O2, H2O, and NO with short cycles.
Operation at 250–350 °C in the specified lean O2/H2O/NO mixture represents transient, low-temperature gasoline or hybrid-vehicle exhaust operation.
Cyclic redox pretreatment will create a nanoscale core–shell structure having an oxidized PGM-rich surface layer around a multi-element alloy core.
Differential oxidation kinetics and thermodynamically driven atom migration during redox cycling selectively segregate PGM atoms to the surface.
The PGM-rich shell supplies optimized adsorption sites for NO and oxygen-containing intermediates.
The multi-principal-element core remains compositionally stable and thereby suppresses sintering and deactivation.
The pretreatment will lower the CO oxidation light-off temperature relative to the untreated catalyst.
The pretreatment will lower the hydrocarbon oxidation light-off temperature relative to the untreated catalyst.
The pretreated catalyst will have greater resistance to thermal aging.
The pretreated catalyst will resist degradation caused by H2O and NO exposure.
The pretreated catalyst will sustain catalytic performance during repeated transient operation.
The intervention will permit lower precious-metal consumption than the untreated starting catalyst.
The untreated high-entropy alloy lacks the engineered surface segregation.
The untreated catalyst has higher light-off temperatures and pronounced transient-exhaust degradation.
The anticipated benefit is bounded to transient lean operation at approximately 250–350 °C.
The long-term persistence of the induced PGM-rich shell under real-world operation and extreme thermal loads is uncertain.
Failure to form or retain the PGM-rich shell, or failure of shell formation to correlate with improved activity versus an untreated control, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The only intervention is a redox pretreatment, with no change in catalyst composition or PGM loading, yet the outcome claims lower precious-metal consumption relative to the untreated starting catalyst. That comparison is not defined consistently unless a lower-PGM formulation is added.
